messages.author: c004b3f72f17eed7
messages.subject: est.map multicore
parts:
Hey!

I'm trying to speed up the generation of the genetic map using the n.cluster argument of the est.map function. It does not produce any errors, but only one core does actual calculation, instead of the number I've requested.
It woks fine with the scanone c.cluster function. Does anyone else have the same issue?

Thank you very much,

Ivan

parts:

Sure.
I've noticed that there is no difference in system.time() between the different number of clusters, so I've tested couple of bigger datasets, where the calculation of the genetic map takes some time. The message on on the package states the right amount of clusters running, but if you observe the actual load on the CPUs, you will notice, that only one is active.

Ivan

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] est.map multicore
parts:
What's going on is that for 5 of your 6 chromosomes, the estimated map is derived almost instantly, and the 6th (chromosome 4) takes a very long time. Since the parallel analysis is to have each CPU work on one chromosome, you don't get any advantage. You see six processes spawned but 5 of the 6 finish almost instantly.

karl
